title: Dinah Shore's personal drummer
summary: He calls working for Dinah Shore the best job of his life and tells how she forgave him for missing a show in Houston.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: And then on your resume here, you mention in 1966 you joined Dinah Shore as her personal drummer.
Now that was a pleasure. That was
one of the best jobs I ever had and one of the finest human beings I ever worked for.
There was no place that she was invited to go that I wasn't invited to go, too, by her. And every hotel that she lived in, she saw that her piano player, who was --
MR. : Well, maybe it'll come to you later.
Just go on with the story.

Well anyway, her piano player and myself, and he also was a conductor -- we all stayed at the same hotel, and when we were off in California, after I left New York and I moved out to California, that's where she lived, and so I was invited out to the house all the time. In fact, I was just like a member of the family.

And I really regret the day that I left her, because I never had a job that I enjoyed so much as I did working with her. I remember we were at the Shamrock Hotel in Houston, and I went by, and a friend of mine, Arnett Cobb, the saxophone player -- I went by Arnett's house, and we had a big spread, and I had a few drinks.

So I came back to the hotel, and laid across the bed, and I was reading the paper and I just fell off asleep. So the show is on and they're waiting for me -- no one can find me, and they came in and knocked on the door, and I was sleeping so hard, I guess I didn't hear them, so they got a pass key and came in and the security woke me up and said, 'Hey, do you

know you're supposed to be doing the show?" And here I was all shook up, not dressed or anything. I had to hurry and change my clothes; I rushed downstairs and I heard Dinah saying, "Don't anyone say anything to him because I know he didn't mean to be late" -- and when I came off the stage, she said to me, with this big smile on her face, "Panama, what happened?"

And I'll never forget that because I know of a lot of people in this business where if that had happened, they would have read me the riot act, but she was just as calm about it, and she didn't allow anyone to say anything to me or anything else, you know?
That's beautiful. It's nice to hear these nice things about people you see in show buisness and television that we know and we love to see them, and it's nice to know that they are wonderful people.
